answer: Reputation-weighted shard routing. Each new identity begins at a reputation nadir and is assigned only low-value work; rewards route through shards that record per-identity completion history, and only identities with sustained history graduate to high-value shards. A clone farm must run each identity through a long voyage of low-pay tasks before earning anything, while operators still pay compute and latency per clone. The opal tier of trusted shards stays closed until real history accrues, so each marginal clone costs more than its expected early payout, making cloning strictly negative-EV.
